title: If Cats Eat Turkey: Boneless and Fully Cooked, Says the ASPCA 🐱 (Things Living In Your House)
description:
Can cats eat turkey? The ASPCA recommends sticking to your pet's normal diet on Thanksgiving. If you do decide to feed your pet a small bite of turkey or other meat, it says to make sure it is boneless and fully cooked. Raw or undercooked turkey may contain salmonella, and poultry bones can be a major choking hazard. The AVMA says plain, boneless, and skinless turkey is generally safe for pets in small portions, but other table scraps, including gravy, sauces, dressing, and meat or poultry fat or skin, can be hard to digest, and sometimes even a small amount can cause pancreatitis. The FDA says not to give high-fat scraps such as skin from a roasted turkey; in cats, pancreatitis symptoms are less clear, such as decreased appetite and weight loss. Onions, garlic and chives can damage red blood cells, and the ASPCA says cats are more susceptible. The ASPCA also says small amounts of lean cooked turkey free of bones and seasoning are okay, and that snacks should be no more than five percent of daily calories — that is their guideline, not a measured serving size. When in doubt, ask your vet.
